title: Conceptual Modeling and Artificial Intelligence: Mutual Benefits from Complementary Worlds
extended_summary:
This paper is an editorial preface to the 3rd International Workshop on Conceptual Modeling Meets Artificial Intelligence (CMAI’2021). It motivates the workshop by arguing that conceptual modeling and data-driven AI are complementary: conceptual modeling offers human-interpretable, explicit, and reproducible representations, whereas AI can efficiently derive patterns from data but often functions as a black box with limited explainability and reproducibility. The paper frames the intersection as an important research area because each field can help mitigate weaknesses in the other.

The main contribution is a conceptual research framework that organizes work at the intersection of conceptual modeling and AI into four categories: exaptation CMAI, CM-driven CMAI, AI-driven CMAI, and CM- & AI-driven CMAI. These categories are presented as a way to position existing and future research, rather than as an empirical intervention or study. The paper briefly summarizes the invited papers in the CMAI’2021 program and maps each to one of these categories.

No human participants, educational setting, or K-12 population are studied in this paper. The article is therefore a theoretical/editorial contribution about research directions and workshop organization, not an evaluation of an AI-powered educational tool. Its conclusion is that combining conceptual modeling and AI can produce mutual benefits by improving explainability, knowledge integration, and the development of AI and modeling methods.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial preface and conceptual workshop overview, not an empirical study. It does not present a tested intervention, comparison design, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct evidence of educational impact, effect sizes, or learner outcomes. Its contribution is conceptual and organizational rather than intervention-based.
